neighbours.label: the verb by which content reaches an audience ('is broadcast to', 'went viral', 'a shot heard round the world', 'was shown to', 'made national headlines'): it predicts the reach that follows (promotes 'global', 'worldwide', 'nationwide'); the same subjects with verbs that do not spread them stay low
fire: The final match was televised to fans in over forty countries.
Within a day, the clip of the dancing goat went viral on every platform.
His speech was heard by listeners across the whole nation.
The scandal made international news within a week.
The documentary was screened to audiences in two hundred cities.
Her post about the lost dog spread across the internet overnight.
The royal wedding was broadcast live around the globe.
The protest footage was seen by millions of people worldwide.
quiet: The final match was cancelled because of the heavy snow.
Within a day, the dancing goat went back to its owner on the farm.
His speech was written on the back of an old envelope.
The scandal made the minister resign within a week.
The documentary was edited in a small studio in Leeds.
Her post about the lost dog was deleted by mistake overnight.
The royal wedding was planned for the first week of June.
The protest footage was stored on an old laptop at home.

notes: probe: 'went viral' 0.760, 'shot heard round the world' 0.722, 'was shown to her family' 0.474, 'broadcast to millions' 0.414, 'made national headlines' 0.274; 'made her nervous' 0.214, 'went home' 0.108, 'concert is held' 0.001. Showing to even a small audience fires, so near misses avoid any dissemination verb
